meta.description: Phase 10 evaluation dataset: 20 questions each for RAG, SQL, RBAC, SECURITY, GENERAL (100 total). Olist-only pivot: the fictional AtliQ company's 7 flat docs_*.md files (and their 10 RAG items, RAG-01..RAG-10) were removed at the user's explicit request, along with the 'hr' RBAC role and the AtliQ-only document departments ('general', 'hr', 'executive' as doc tags) it depended on. Every remaining item, and every replacement item, is grounded in either the real Olist-generated RAG documents (scripts/generate_olist_rag_docs.py) or the real data/olist.db schema.
ground_truth_policy: RAG items: 'expected_sources' entries are either exact filenames or fnmatch glob patterns for the Olist-generated docs, whose exact numeric content depends on live data the assistant could not execute/verify itself. 'reference' is null for all RAG items in this dataset (no legacy verbatim-quoted source docs remain post-pivot) -- evaluation/run_evaluation.py must skip RAGAS context_precision/context_recall for these null-reference items rather than fabricate a reference. Exact record-id filenames for regional_summary (state abbreviations) and payment_summary (payment types) are chosen from real, well-documented Olist dataset values (Brazilian state codes; payment_type in {credit_card, boleto, voucher, debit_card}), but -- like RAG-11..RAG-20 before them -- have not been execution-verified against the actual generated files in this repo.

SQL items: 'reference_sql' is a hand-written correct query. Ground truth is NOT a hand-typed number -- the harness executes reference_sql itself at evaluation time against the real data/olist.db and compares that live result to the pipeline's own generated-SQL result. This was an explicit user decision (see conversation) specifically to avoid the assistant fabricating Olist data values it cannot compute without running code.

RBAC items: 'expected_allowed' is derived directly from config.py's ROLE_ACCESS / SQL_TABLE_ACCESS dictionaries as they exist in the repo, hand-traced against those dictionaries before being written here. Updated for the Olist-only pivot's RBAC redesign (no 'hr' role; document departments are now sales/products/payments/revenue/sellers/delivery/orders only).
SECURITY items: 'expected_blocked' / 'expected_pii_types' are checked against guardrails.py's real detection functions, not against a subjective judgment call.

GENERAL items: 'expected_out_of_scope' distinguishes true out-of-scope/small-talk questions from in-scope control questions (included so the eval also catches OVER-refusal, not just under-refusal). In-scope control questions were rewritten for the Olist pivot and assigned to roles that actually have document access to the relevant department, so a correct refusal-avoidance depends on the question being in-scope, not on RBAC also happening to deny it.

items.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM orders

items.question: What is the average price of items sold, across all order items?
items.reference_sql: SELECT AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM order_items

items.question: How many distinct customers (unique people) are there?
items.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS num_customers FROM customers

items.question: How many orders have the status 'delivered'?
items.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_delivered FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'delivered'

items.question: What is the average delivery_days for orders that were delivered on time?
items.reference_sql: SELECT AVG(delivery_days) AS avg_days FROM orders WHERE delivery_status = 'on_time'

items.question: How many sellers are located in the state of SP?
items.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_sellers FROM sellers WHERE seller_state = 'SP'

items.question: What is the total freight value across all order items?
items.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(freight_value) AS total_freight FROM order_items

items.question: How many distinct product categories are there (English names)?
items.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT product_category_name_english) AS num_categories FROM categories

items.question: What is the average review score across all reviews?
items.reference_sql: SELECT AVG(review_score) AS avg_score FROM reviews

items.question: How many orders were canceled?
items.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_canceled FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'canceled'

items.question: What is the total payment value collected via credit card?
items.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(payment_value) AS total FROM payments WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card'

items.question: How many payment records used more than 1 installment?
items.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num FROM payments WHERE payment_installments > 1

items.question: What is the total revenue (price plus freight) generated by sellers based in Rio de Janeiro (RJ)?
items.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(oi.price + oi.freight_value) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN sellers s ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id WHERE s.seller_state = 'RJ'

items.question: What is the average payment value across all payment records?
items.reference_sql: SELECT AVG(payment_value) AS avg_payment FROM payments

items.question: How many reviews had a 5-star score?
items.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num FROM reviews WHERE review_score = 5

items.question: What is the maximum item price recorded in order items?
items.reference_sql: SELECT MAX(price) AS max_price FROM order_items

items.question: How many products are in the products table in total?
items.reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_products FROM products

items.question: What is the average product weight in grams across all products?
items.reference_sql: SELECT AVG(product_weight_g) AS avg_weight FROM products

items.question: Using order facts, what is the total revenue (price plus freight) for orders from customers in the state of MG?
items.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(price + freight_value) AS total_revenue FROM order_facts WHERE customer_state = 'MG'

items.question: What is the total payment value collected via boleto payments?
items.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(payment_value) AS total FROM payments WHERE payment_type = 'boleto'
